251	async def _apply_transfer(
252	    session: AsyncSession,
253	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
254	    item: Item,
255	    move: StockMove,
256	    qty: Decimal,
257	    method: CostingMethod,
258	    currency_code: str,
259	    from_warehouse_id: uuid.UUID | None,
260	    to_warehouse_id: uuid.UUID | None,
261	) -> CostingResult:
262	    """TRANSFER carries cost at the current valuation. Within ONE warehouse it is fully
263	    value-neutral — the valuation/layers don't change and NO journal is posted (D-037). Between
264	    warehouses the value moves WITH the stock (issue from source at current cost, receive into dest
265	    at that same cost) but, because both warehouses share the one inventory account in v1, the net
266	    journal is still zero — so a transfer never publishes a StockValued event. The computed transfer
267	    unit cost is still written onto the move for the ledger."""
268	    if from_warehouse_id is None or to_warehouse_id is None:
269	        raise ValidationFailedError(
270	            message="A transfer needs both warehouses to value",
271	            code="inventory.costing_transfer_sides",
272	            details={"move_id": str(move.id)},
273	        )
274	    if from_warehouse_id == to_warehouse_id:
275	        # Same warehouse: only the bin changed; value is unchanged. Carry the current cost onto the
276	        # move for the ledger, touch nothing else, post no journal.
277	        move.unit_cost = await _current_unit_cost(
278	            session, tenant_id, item, from_warehouse_id, method
279	        )
280	        return CostingResult(unit_cost=move.unit_cost, event=None)
281	
282	    # Cross-warehouse: remove value from the source and add it to the destination at the SAME cost,
283	    # so the value follows the stock between warehouses while the net GL effect is nil.
284	    if method == CostingMethod.MOVING_AVERAGE:
285	        cost, _residual = await costing_mav.mav_issue(
286	            session, tenant_id, item.id, from_warehouse_id, qty, currency_code
287	        )
288	        unit_cost = (cost / qty) if qty > 0 else Decimal(0)
289	        await costing_mav.mav_receive(
290	            session, tenant_id, item.id, to_warehouse_id, qty, unit_cost
291	        )
292	    else:
293	        cost = await costing_fifo.consume_layers(
294	            session,
295	            tenant_id,
296	            item_id=item.id,
297	            warehouse_id=from_warehouse_id,
298	            issue_move_id=move.id,
299	            qty=qty,
300	            currency_code=currency_code,
301	        )
302	        unit_cost = (cost / qty) if qty > 0 else Decimal(0)
303	        await costing_fifo.create_layer(
304	            session,
305	            tenant_id,
306	            item_id=item.id,
307	            warehouse_id=to_warehouse_id,
308	            receipt_move_id=move.id,
309	            received_at=move.move_date,
310	            qty=qty,
311	            unit_cost=unit_cost,
312	        )
313	    move.unit_cost = unit_cost
314	    return CostingResult(unit_cost=unit_cost, event=None)

317	async def _current_unit_cost(
318	    session: AsyncSession,
319	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
320	    item: Item,
321	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID,
322	    method: CostingMethod,
323	) -> Decimal:
324	    """The current per-unit cost of an (item, warehouse) for a value-neutral transfer's ledger
325	    entry:
326	    the moving-average avg, or the FIFO weighted average of the live layers. Reads only (no
327	    writes)."""
328	    if method == CostingMethod.MOVING_AVERAGE:
329	        return await costing_mav.mav_avg_cost(session, tenant_id, item.id, warehouse_id)
330	    return await costing_mav.fifo_weighted_cost(session, tenant_id, item.id, warehouse_id)

1	"""Inventory VALUATION tables — the value single source of truth (PLAN 5.3, D-020/D-037).
2	
3	The move ledger (``inv_stock_moves``) and the quant projection (``inv_stock_quants``) remain the
4	QUANTITY SSOT; these three tables are the VALUE SSOT, updated in the SAME transaction as every move
5	(D-037). Which engine a (item, warehouse) uses is the item's ``costing_method``:
6	
7	- ``ItemValuation`` (``inv_item_valuations``) — the MOVING-AVERAGE state per (item, warehouse):
8	  on_hand_qty, avg_unit_cost (full precision) and total_value, with ``UNIQUE(tenant, item,
9	  warehouse)`` as the upsert/lock target and ``CHECK(on_hand_qty >= 0)`` (value and quantity never
10	  disagree — the zero-quantity flush keeps total_value at 0 exactly when on_hand hits 0, D-020).
11	- ``CostLayer`` (``inv_cost_layers``) — one FIFO layer per RECEIPT: original_qty, remaining_qty
12	  (``CHECK 0 <= remaining_qty <= original_qty``) and unit_cost, keyed back to its
13	  ``receipt_move_id`` and ordered by ``received_at`` then id. Issues consume the oldest first.
14	- ``LayerConsumption`` (``inv_layer_consumptions``) — one row per layer an ISSUE touches: qty +
15	  cost. The audit trail AND the exact-reversal record (reversing an issue replays these rows
16	  backward onto the same layers, restoring remaining_qty — D-020).
17	
18	Valuation is per (item, WAREHOUSE), not per bin: transfers within one warehouse are value-neutral
19	(no journal), while a transfer BETWEEN warehouses moves value with the stock (D-037). All tables
20	follow the D-007 composite-tenant-FK backstop (``tenant_unique()`` + ``tenant_fk()`` composites) so
21	a child can never point at another tenant's parent. Enum-free; money/quantity are MoneyType/
22	QuantityType (exact on both engines, D-015). NOT AuditMixin — valuation is a derived projection of
23	the audited moves (the quant-table reasoning, D-036); auditing it too would double-record.
24	"""
25	
26	import uuid
27	from datetime import date
28	from decimal import Decimal
29	
30	import sqlalchemy as sa
31	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
32	
33	from app.core.models import (
34	    Base,
35	    TenantMixin,
36	    TimestampMixin,
37	    UuidPKMixin,
38	    tenant_fk,
39	    tenant_unique,
40	)
41	from app.core.money import MoneyType, QuantityType
42	
43	
44	class ItemValuation(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
45	    """The MOVING-AVERAGE valuation state per (item, warehouse) (D-020/D-037).
46	
47	    Maintained in the move transaction under ``with_for_update`` (PG row lock serializing concurrent
48	    movers; SQLite no-op + single-writer lock, D-020): a RECEIPT adds ``qty × unit_cost`` to
49	    total_value and recomputes ``avg_unit_cost = total_value / on_hand_qty`` UNROUNDED (full scale-6
50	    precision, so successive issues don't drift); an ISSUE subtracts ``quantize(qty × avg)`` and,
51	    when on_hand_qty reaches exactly 0, FLUSHES the residual total_value to the price-difference
52	    account so value and quantity never disagree. The ``CHECK(on_hand_qty >= 0)`` backs the
53	    no-negative-stock rule on the value side (D-020). ``UNIQUE(tenant, item, warehouse)`` is the
54	    upsert + lock target."""
55	
56	    __tablename__ = "inv_item_valuations"
57	    __table_args__ = (
58	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
59	            "tenant_id",
60	            "item_id",
61	            "warehouse_id",
62	            name="uq_inv_item_valuations_tenant_id_item_id_warehouse_id",
63	        ),
64	        tenant_unique(),
65	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
66	        tenant_fk("inv_items", "item_id"),
67	        tenant_fk("inv_warehouses", "warehouse_id"),
68	        # Negative on-hand forbidden on the value side too (D-020) — portable single-column CHECK.
69	        sa.CheckConstraint("on_hand_qty >= 0", name="on_hand_non_negative"),
70	        sa.Index(
71	            "ix_inv_item_valuations_tenant_id_item_id", "tenant_id", "item_id"
72	        ),
73	    )
74	
75	    item_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
76	    warehouse_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
77	    on_hand_qty: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(QuantityType(), nullable=False)
78	    # Full-precision average (D-015: MoneyType keeps scale 6) — never quantized to currency dp, so
79	    # repeated issues do not accumulate rounding drift; only the POSTED COGS rounds (zero-qty
80	    # flush).
81	    avg_unit_cost: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(MoneyType(), nullable=False)
82	    total_value: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(MoneyType(), nullable=False)
83	
84	
85	class CostLayer(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
86	    """A FIFO cost layer (D-020): one per RECEIPT (or positive ADJUSTMENT) into a (item, warehouse).
87	
88	    Created with ``original_qty == remaining_qty == qty`` at the receipt's ``unit_cost``; issues
89	    consume layers oldest-first by ``(received_at, id)`` under ``with_for_update``, decrementing
90	    ``remaining_qty``. The ``CHECK(remaining_qty >= 0 AND remaining_qty <= original_qty)`` makes a
91	    layer's consumed amount well-defined on both engines (D-020). ``receipt_move_id`` is a
92	    composite tenant FK back to the move that created it, so reversing that RECEIPT can find and
93	    zero its layer (only valid while the layer is unconsumed). The
94	    ``(tenant, item, warehouse, received_at)`` index serves the FIFO consumption scan
95	    (PERFORMANCE §1)."""
96	
97	    __tablename__ = "inv_cost_layers"
98	    __table_args__ = (
99	        tenant_unique(),
100	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
101	        tenant_fk("inv_items", "item_id"),
102	        tenant_fk("inv_warehouses", "warehouse_id"),
103	        tenant_fk("inv_stock_moves", "receipt_move_id"),
104	        sa.CheckConstraint(
105	            "remaining_qty >= 0 AND remaining_qty <= original_qty",
106	            name="remaining_within_original",
107	        ),
108	        # The FIFO consumption scan reads a (item, warehouse)'s layers oldest-first (PERF §1).
109	        sa.Index(
110	            "ix_inv_cost_layers_tenant_id_item_id_warehouse_id_received_at",
111	            "tenant_id",
112	            "item_id",
113	            "warehouse_id",
114	            "received_at",
115	        ),
116	        # FK index for "this receipt move's layer" (the receipt-reversal lookup).
117	        sa.Index(
118	            "ix_inv_cost_layers_tenant_id_receipt_move_id",
119	            "tenant_id",
120	            "receipt_move_id",
121	        ),
122	    )
123	
124	    item_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
125	    warehouse_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
126	    receipt_move_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
127	    # Date the layer was received — the FIFO ordering key (id breaks same-date ties). A Date (not
128	    # datetime) suffices: ordering is (received_at, id) and id is the within-day tiebreaker.
129	    received_at: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
130	    original_qty: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(QuantityType(), nullable=False)
131	    remaining_qty: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(QuantityType(), nullable=False)
132	    unit_cost: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(MoneyType(), nullable=False)
133	
134	
135	class LayerConsumption(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
136	    """One layer an ISSUE consumed (D-020): qty drawn from the layer + the cost charged for it.
137	
138	    One row per (issue_move, layer) touched — the per-layer COGS audit trail AND the exact-reversal
139	    record: reversing an issue replays these rows backward, ADDING ``qty`` back to each named
140	    layer's remaining_qty (restoring the exact FIFO state), so a reversal is replay, never recompute
141	    (D-020).
142	    Composite tenant FKs to both the issue move and the layer keep the link tenant-safe."""
143	
144	    __tablename__ = "inv_layer_consumptions"
145	    __table_args__ = (
146	        tenant_unique(),
147	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
148	        tenant_fk("inv_stock_moves", "issue_move_id"),
149	        tenant_fk("inv_cost_layers", "layer_id"),
150	        # "This issue's consumptions" (reversal replay) and "this layer's consumptions" — both
151	        # FK-indexed (PERFORMANCE §1).
152	        sa.Index(
153	            "ix_inv_layer_consumptions_tenant_id_issue_move_id",
154	            "tenant_id",
155	            "issue_move_id",
156	        ),
157	        sa.Index(
158	            "ix_inv_layer_consumptions_tenant_id_layer_id", "tenant_id", "layer_id"
159	        ),
160	    )
161	
162	    issue_move_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
163	    layer_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
164	    qty: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(QuantityType(), nullable=False)
165	    cost: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(MoneyType(), nullable=False)
166	
167	
168	__all__ = ["CostLayer", "ItemValuation", "LayerConsumption"]

1	"""Domain events inventory PUBLISHES (D-011/D-020). Declarative data only — no logic, no models —
2	so finance's ``handlers.py`` may import these typed classes (the STRUCTURE §5 events.py allowance,
3	explicitly covering finance importing "upward" from inventory because events carry no behaviour).
4	
5	``StockValued`` is fired inside ``create_move`` AFTER the move + quant + valuation/layer updates,
6	carrying the computed value delta and the THREE GL account ids resolved from the item's category at
7	publish time (D-029 opaque ids). ``finance/handlers.py`` subscribes and posts the COGS/inventory
8	journal in the SAME transaction (D-011/D-020), so the move and its journal commit or roll back as
9	one
10	— a stock move can never exist without its journal entry, or vice versa.
11	
12	ONE event for every value-changing move; the handler branches on ``move_type`` for the per-type
13	postings (RECEIPT / ISSUE / ADJUSTMENT up/down). A value-neutral within-warehouse TRANSFER does NOT
14	publish (no value change → no journal). All amounts are full-precision Decimals; the handler
15	quantizes
16	the posted COGS to the currency's decimals (D-015).
17	"""
18	
19	import uuid
20	from decimal import Decimal
21	from typing import ClassVar
22	
23	from app.core.events import DomainEvent
24	from app.modules.inventory.constants import STOCK_VALUED_EVENT_KEY
25	
26	
27	class StockValued(DomainEvent):
28	    """A stock move changed valuation (D-020). Payload:
29	
30	    - ``move_id`` + ``move_date`` + ``move_number`` — the driving move (the journal posts with
31	      ``move_date``; a date in a CLOSED period makes the journal's period trigger fire inside the
32	      same transaction, rolling the whole move back — you cannot move stock into a closed period).
33	    - ``move_type`` — RECEIPT / ISSUE / ADJUSTMENT (the handler branches on it; TRANSFER within one
34	      warehouse never publishes). ``is_inbound`` disambiguates an ADJUSTMENT's direction (increase
35	      vs decrease) since both carry move_type ADJUSTMENT.
36	    - ``item_id`` + ``warehouse_id`` + ``quantity`` — the dimensions copied onto the COGS journal
37	      line (item dimension) and the value context.
38	    - ``total_cost`` — the value Δ the move moved (positive): RECEIPT entry value, ISSUE/decrease
39	      computed COGS, increase value. ``residual_to_price_difference`` is the moving-average
40	      zero-quantity flush amount (signed, usually 0) the handler posts to price-difference WITHIN
41	      the issue's entry so value and quantity never disagree (D-020).
42	    - ``document_id`` — the move's core_documents id (the docflow source ref the handler links the
43	      journal entry to, link_type 'posts').
44	    - ``inventory_account_id`` + ``offset_account_id`` — the two legs of the main posting: inventory
45	      is always one side; the OFFSET is chosen by the costing engine per move type (ISSUE -> COGS;
46	      RECEIPT / ADJUSTMENT -> price-difference; a reversal -> the OPPOSITE of the original move's

1	"""Moving-average costing mechanics (PLAN 5.3, D-020): the ``inv_item_valuations`` row math, split
2	from ``costing.py`` to keep both <400 lines (the FIFO half is ``costing_fifo.py``).
3	
4	This file owns ONLY the moving-average state updates + the current-cost reads; the orchestration and
5	reversal sequencing live in ``costing.py``. Every function runs in the move's transaction and locks
6	the (item, warehouse) row ``with_for_update`` (PG row lock serializing concurrent movers; SQLite
7	no-op + single-writer lock, D-020).
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import uuid
13	from decimal import Decimal
14	
15	from sqlalchemy import select
16	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
17	
18	from app.core.exceptions import ValidationFailedError
19	from app.core.money import quantize_for_currency
20	from app.modules.inventory.models import CostLayer, ItemValuation
21	
22	
23	async def locked_valuation(
24	    session: AsyncSession,
25	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
26	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
27	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID,
28	) -> ItemValuation | None:
29	    """Load the (item, warehouse) moving-average row FOR UPDATE (PG lock serializing movers; SQLite
30	    no-op, D-020), or None if it does not exist yet."""
31	    stmt = (
32	        select(ItemValuation)
33	        .where(
34	            ItemValuation.tenant_id == tenant_id,
35	            ItemValuation.item_id == item_id,
36	            ItemValuation.warehouse_id == warehouse_id,
37	        )
38	        .with_for_update()
39	    )
40	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
41	
42	
43	async def mav_receive(
44	    session: AsyncSession,
45	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
46	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
47	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID,
48	    qty: Decimal,
49	    unit_cost: Decimal,
50	) -> None:
51	    """Moving-average RECEIPT (D-020): total_value += qty × unit_cost; on_hand += qty; avg =
52	    total_value / on_hand UNROUNDED (full precision, so issues don't drift)."""
53	    valuation = await locked_valuation(session, tenant_id, item_id, warehouse_id)
54	    receipt_value = qty * unit_cost
55	    if valuation is None:
56	        session.add(
57	            ItemValuation(
58	                tenant_id=tenant_id,
59	                item_id=item_id,
60	                warehouse_id=warehouse_id,
61	                on_hand_qty=qty,
62	                avg_unit_cost=unit_cost,
63	                total_value=receipt_value,
64	            )
65	        )
66	        await session.flush()
67	        return
68	    new_qty = Decimal(valuation.on_hand_qty) + qty
69	    new_value = Decimal(valuation.total_value) + receipt_value
70	    valuation.on_hand_qty = new_qty
71	    valuation.total_value = new_value
72	    valuation.avg_unit_cost = new_value / new_qty if new_qty > 0 else Decimal(0)
73	    await session.flush()
74	
75	
76	async def mav_issue(
77	    session: AsyncSession,
78	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
79	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
80	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID,
81	    qty: Decimal,
82	    currency_code: str,
83	) -> tuple[Decimal, Decimal]:
84	    """Moving-average ISSUE (D-020): cogs = quantize(qty × avg, currency dp, HALF_UP); total_value
85	    -=
86	    cogs; on_hand -= qty. When on_hand hits exactly 0 the residual total_value is FLUSHED — returned
87	    as the signed price-difference amount so value and quantity never disagree. Returns (cogs,
88	    residual_flush)."""
89	    valuation = await locked_valuation(session, tenant_id, item_id, warehouse_id)
90	    if valuation is None:
91	        # The 5.2 quant pre-flight guarantees stock exists, so a missing valuation is a
92	        # costing/quant divergence — never reachable on the happy path.
93	        raise ValidationFailedError(
94	            message="No moving-average valuation exists for the issued stock",
95	            code="inventory.costing_valuation_missing",
96	            details={"item_id": str(item_id), "warehouse_id": str(warehouse_id)},
97	        )
98	    cogs = quantize_for_currency(qty * Decimal(valuation.avg_unit_cost), currency_code)
99	    new_qty = Decimal(valuation.on_hand_qty) - qty
100	    residual_flush = Decimal(0)
101	    if new_qty <= 0:
102	        # On-hand hit (exactly) zero: flush whatever total_value remains after removing this COGS so
103	        # the row lands at value 0 with quantity 0 (D-020 — rounding drift absorbed here). A
104	        # positive
105	        # residual means leftover value (Dr price-difference); negative means over-issued value.
106	        residual_flush = Decimal(valuation.total_value) - cogs
107	        valuation.on_hand_qty = Decimal(0)
108	        valuation.total_value = Decimal(0)
109	        # avg_unit_cost is left as-is (meaningless at zero stock; the next receipt resets it).
110	    else:
111	        valuation.on_hand_qty = new_qty
112	        valuation.total_value = Decimal(valuation.total_value) - cogs
113	    await session.flush()
114	    return cogs, residual_flush
115	
116	
117	async def mav_avg_cost(
118	    session: AsyncSession,
119	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
120	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
121	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID,
122	) -> Decimal:
123	    """The current moving-average unit cost of an (item, warehouse), or 0 if none — used for a
124	    value-neutral within-warehouse transfer's ledger row (no write)."""
125	    valuation = await locked_valuation(session, tenant_id, item_id, warehouse_id)
126	    return Decimal(valuation.avg_unit_cost) if valuation is not None else Decimal(0)
127	
128	
129	async def fifo_weighted_cost(
130	    session: AsyncSession,
131	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
132	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
133	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID,
134	) -> Decimal:
135	    """The weighted-average cost of an (item, warehouse)'s LIVE FIFO layers (Σ value / Σ qty), or 0
136	    if none — used for a value-neutral within-warehouse transfer's ledger row (no write). The qty ×
137	    cost product is summed in PYTHON (each factor already a typed Decimal), never ``func.sum(qty ×
138	    cost)`` — multiplying two scaled-integer columns on SQLite yields a ×10^12 value the MoneyType
139	    result processor cannot un-scale (D-015 trigger discipline)."""
140	    rows = (
141	        await session.execute(
142	            select(CostLayer.remaining_qty, CostLayer.unit_cost).where(
143	                CostLayer.tenant_id == tenant_id,
144	                CostLayer.item_id == item_id,
145	                CostLayer.warehouse_id == warehouse_id,
146	                CostLayer.remaining_qty > 0,
147	            )
148	        )
149	    ).all()
150	    total_qty = sum((Decimal(qty) for qty, _cost in rows), Decimal(0))
151	    total_value = sum((Decimal(qty) * Decimal(cost) for qty, cost in rows), Decimal(0))
152	    return (total_value / total_qty) if total_qty > 0 else Decimal(0)
153

38	async def list_moves(
39	    session: AsyncSession,
40	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
41	    *,
42	    filters: StockMoveFilter,
43	    cursor: str | None = None,
44	    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
45	) -> Page[StockMove]:
46	    """Keyset-paginated move ledger (D-014), newest first by (move_date DESC, id). Filters narrow by
47	    item, bin (either side), type and date range and fold into the cursor fingerprint so a cursor
48	    cannot bleed across filtered views. The append-only ledger view procurement/sales audit from."""
49	    stmt = select(StockMove).where(StockMove.tenant_id == tenant_id)
50	    if filters.item_id is not None:
51	        stmt = stmt.where(StockMove.item_id == filters.item_id)
52	    if filters.bin_id is not None:
53	        stmt = stmt.where(
54	            (StockMove.from_bin_id == filters.bin_id)
55	            | (StockMove.to_bin_id == filters.bin_id)
56	        )
57	    if filters.move_type is not None:
58	        stmt = stmt.where(StockMove.move_type == MoveType(filters.move_type).value)
59	    if filters.date_from is not None:
60	        stmt = stmt.where(StockMove.move_date >= filters.date_from)
61	    if filters.date_to is not None:
62	        stmt = stmt.where(StockMove.move_date <= filters.date_to)
63	
64	    fingerprint = filter_fingerprint(
65	        filters.item_id,
66	        filters.bin_id,
67	        filters.move_type,
68	        filters.date_from,
69	        filters.date_to,
70	    )

72	        session,
73	        stmt,

75	        # same-date moves order deterministically. move_date is an immutable Date (no SQLite
76	        # fractional-seconds keyset hazard, unlike created_at — D-033).
77	        order_by=[OrderKey(StockMove.move_date, SortDirection.DESC)],
78	        pk=StockMove.id,

1	"""Finance domain-event handlers (D-011) — the FIRST real cross-module handler (PLAN 5.3, D-020).
2	
3	Subscribes to ``inventory.stock.valued`` and posts the COGS/inventory valuation journal in the SAME
4	transaction as the stock move (D-011 run_in_uow drains before commit; D-020 same-transaction COGS).
5	Because the handler shares the session and any handler exception rolls the WHOLE transaction back, a
6	stock move can never commit without its journal entry, or vice versa — the load-bearing atomicity
7	invariant. The journal posts with the move's ``move_date``: a date in a CLOSED period makes the
8	journal's period trigger fire inside this same transaction, which rolls the whole move back (you
9	cannot move stock into a closed accounting period — correct by construction).
10	
11	Postings per move type (the GL effect of each — D-020). The costing engine pre-selects the OFFSET
12	account per type and the event carries it, so the handler is a thin Dr/Cr direction switch:
13	- RECEIPT / ADJUSTMENT-up: Dr inventory / Cr price-difference. A STANDALONE receipt (opening
14	  balance, manual stock-in) has no procurement GR clearing yet, so its offset is price-difference /
15	  inventory-adjustment account; procurement's goods-receipt path (6.x) will OVERRIDE this with its
16	  own GR/IR offset. ADJUSTMENT-up is the same shape (a stock increase with no document behind it).
17	- ISSUE: Dr COGS / Cr inventory at the computed cost (goods left for sale/production).
18	- ADJUSTMENT-down: Dr price-difference / Cr inventory (an inventory write-off, no document).
19	- The moving-average zero-quantity FLUSH posts its residual to price-difference WITHIN the issue's
20	  entry so value and quantity never disagree (D-020).
21	- A reversal posts the EXACT reverse of the original move's entry (reversing an issue credits COGS;
22	  reversing a receipt debits price-difference) — the costing engine sets the reversal's offset.
23	- TRANSFER within one inventory account: value-neutral → the inventory engine publishes NO event, so
24	  the handler never runs for it (documented; no journal).
25	
26	The journal is built through the finance posting service (``create_draft_entry`` + ``post_entry``),
27	NEVER raw inserts, so every journal invariant (balance, one-side CHECK, period, immutability,
28	numbering, audit, docflow) fires exactly as for any posting. The move's document is linked to the
29	journal entry's document ('posts' edge) so the docflow viewer shows move -> COGS entry.
30	
31	Registration: ``app.main.register_event_handlers`` subscribes ``post_stock_valuation_journal`` to
32	the
33	event key at the app factory (the deterministic D-011 registration seam), so the test harness can
34	re-register after its per-test ``clear_subscriptions`` reset (D-025) without a module re-import.
35	"""
36	
37	from __future__ import annotations
38	
39	import uuid
40	from datetime import date
41	from decimal import Decimal
42	
43	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
44	
45	from app.core import docflow
46	from app.core.money import quantize_for_currency
47	from app.modules.finance import queries as finance_queries
48	from app.modules.finance.constants import DocumentType
49	from app.modules.finance.schemas import JournalEntryCreate, JournalLineCreate
50	from app.modules.finance.service.journal import create_draft_entry, post_entry
51	from app.modules.inventory.constants import DEFAULT_COSTING_CURRENCY, STOCK_MOVE_POSTS_LINK
52	from app.modules.inventory.events import StockValued
53	
54	# A signed posting: (account_id, amount). Positive amount => debit, negative => credit. The line
55	# builder drops zeros and splits into the journal's one-sided debit/credit lines.
56	_SignedPosting = tuple[uuid.UUID, Decimal]
57	
58	
59	async def post_stock_valuation_journal(session: AsyncSession, event: StockValued) -> None:
60	    """Post the COGS/inventory journal for a valued stock move (D-020), in the move's transaction.
61	
62	    Registered via ``app.main.register_event_handlers`` (the deterministic D-011 registration seam),
63	    not an import-time ``@on`` decorator, so the test harness can re-register it after its per-test
64	    ``clear_subscriptions`` reset (D-025) without relying on a module re-import.
65	
66	    Builds the signed postings for the move type, turns them into balanced one-sided journal lines,
67	    posts a COGS-typed entry dated the move date (the period trigger fires here — a closed period
68	    rolls the whole move back), and links move.document -> entry.document ('posts')."""
69	    currency_code = (
70	        await finance_queries.functional_currency_or_none(session, event.tenant_id)
71	        or DEFAULT_COSTING_CURRENCY
72	    )
73	    # total_cost is already quantized for ISSUE (per-layer / MAV quantize) but a RECEIPT's
74	    # qty × unit_cost can carry sub-currency digits — quantize the posted amount at the boundary
75	    # (D-015); the residual flush is already an exact MoneyType difference.
76	    amount = quantize_for_currency(Decimal(event.total_cost), currency_code)
77	    residual = Decimal(event.residual_to_price_difference)
78	
79	    postings = _postings_for(event, amount, residual)
80	    lines = _lines_from_postings(postings, event.item_id)
81	    if len(lines) < 2:
82	        # A zero-value move (e.g. a free receipt) produces no balanced entry — nothing to post. The
83	        # quant/valuation still updated; there is simply no GL effect. (Not reachable on priced
84	        # moves.)
85	        return
86	
87	    entry = await create_draft_entry(
88	        session,
89	        event.tenant_id,
90	        JournalEntryCreate(
91	            posting_date=date.fromisoformat(event.move_date),
92	            currency_code=currency_code,
93	            description=f"Stock {event.move_type.lower()} {event.move_number}",
94	            document_type=DocumentType.COGS,
95	            lines=lines,
96	        ),
97	    )
98	    await post_entry(session, event.tenant_id, entry.id)
99	    # Link the move's document to the journal entry's document so the docflow chain shows the COGS
100	    # posting (D-012 'posts' edge — the finance posting convention).
101	    await docflow.link_documents(
102	        session,
103	        event.tenant_id,
104	        predecessor=event.document_id,
105	        successor=entry.document_id,
106	        link_type=STOCK_MOVE_POSTS_LINK,
107	    )
108	
109	
110	def _postings_for(
111	    event: StockValued, amount: Decimal, residual: Decimal
112	) -> list[_SignedPosting]:
113	    """The signed GL postings (positive = debit, negative = credit) for the move (D-020).
114	
115	    The costing engine already chose ``offset_account_id`` per move type (ISSUE -> COGS; RECEIPT /
116	    ADJUSTMENT -> price-difference; a reversal -> the opposite of the original's offset), so the
117	    handler stays a thin Dr/Cr direction switch:
118	    - inbound: Dr inventory / Cr offset (stock entered or an issue was reversed).
119	    - outbound: Dr offset / Cr inventory (stock left or a receipt was reversed). The inventory leg
120	      additionally carries the moving-average zero-quantity residual, flushed to price-difference,
121	      so value and quantity reconcile to zero (D-020). ``residual`` is 0 unless the issue drove
122	      on-hand to exactly zero."""
123	    if event.is_inbound:
124	        return [
125	            (event.inventory_account_id, amount),
126	            (event.offset_account_id, -amount),
127	        ]
128	    return [
129	        (event.offset_account_id, amount),
130	        (event.inventory_account_id, -(amount + residual)),
131	        (event.price_difference_account_id, residual),
132	    ]
133	
134	
135	def _lines_from_postings(
136	    postings: list[_SignedPosting], item_id: uuid.UUID
137	) -> list[JournalLineCreate]:
138	    """Collapse signed postings per account, drop zeros, and emit one-sided journal lines (D-017):
139	    a positive net is a debit, a negative net a credit. The item dimension rides every line so the
140	    COGS entry is attributable to the item (D-017 dimensions)."""
141	    net: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal] = {}
142	    for account_id, signed in postings:
143	        net[account_id] = net.get(account_id, Decimal(0)) + signed
144	    lines: list[JournalLineCreate] = []
145	    for account_id, value in net.items():
146	        if value == 0:
147	            continue
148	        if value > 0:
149	            lines.append(
150	                JournalLineCreate(
151	                    account_id=account_id,
152	                    transaction_debit_amount=value,
153	                    item_id=item_id,
154	                )
155	            )
156	        else:
157	            lines.append(
158	                JournalLineCreate(
159	                    account_id=account_id,
160	                    transaction_credit_amount=-value,
161	                    item_id=item_id,
162	                )
163	            )
164	    return lines
165	
166	
167	__all__ = ["post_stock_valuation_journal"]

2	
3	Long-running operations (FX revaluation, payment runs, statement imports >1k lines, MRP) must
4	never execute inside a request that can hit a proxy timeout. The pattern:
5	
6	1. A module registers a handler at import time::
7	
8	       @register_job("finance.fx_revaluation")
9	       async def handler(session, tenant_id, payload: dict) -> dict: ...
10	
11	   The registry is CODE-DEFINED, exactly like the permission registry (core/rbac.py): a job type
12	   exists because a handler for it is in the codebase, never as data.
13	2. The endpoint calls ``submit_job(session, ...)`` INSIDE its ``run_in_uow`` work — the PENDING
14	   row commits atomically with the request (and with the D-013 idempotency capture, so a replayed
15	   Idempotency-Key returns the SAME job id) — then, strictly AFTER the uow commit, calls
16	   ``schedule_job(job.id, session_factory)`` and returns ``202 {job_id, status}``.
17	3. The client polls ``GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}`` (core/jobs_router.py) until COMPLETED/FAILED.
18	
19	**The runner** (``_execute_job``) opens its OWN session from the factory the submitter passed —
20	in production that is the request's ``get_session_factory`` dependency (the app factory), in
21	tests the per-test-engine factory the conftest override injects, so the runner always lands in
22	the same database as the submit. It restores the submitting context: ``tenant_context(tenant_id)``
23	(D-007 — handler reads/writes are tenant-filtered and stamped) and the D-010 actor ContextVar from
24	``submitted_by_user_id`` (handler writes are audited with the submitting user as actor). It marks
25	RUNNING (own commit), then runs the handler inside ``run_in_uow`` so domain events + audit behave
26	EXACTLY as in-request; the COMPLETED status + result are set inside the same uow, so business
27	writes and the terminal status commit atomically. On any exception the uow rolls the work back
28	and the runner commits only the FAILED status + error string.
29	
30	**Scheduling happens post-commit by contract** (the router calls ``schedule_job`` after
31	``run_in_uow`` returns), so the runner never races the submitting transaction's visibility.
32	
33	**Concurrency cap:** at most ``MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS`` handlers run at once (an asyncio semaphore,
34	created lazily PER EVENT LOOP because asyncio primitives bind to their first loop and tests run
35	one loop per test), so a burst of jobs cannot starve the event loop or the DB pool.
36	
37	**Swap seam:** submitters call ``schedule_job``, which delegates to the module ``scheduler``
38	bound to the ``JobScheduler`` Protocol — the same pattern as the D-011 event bus singleton. A
39	real queue (arq/celery) replaces that one binding (its ``schedule`` enqueues the job id and its
40	workers own their own engine, ignoring ``session_factory``) with zero submitter changes.
41	
42	**Not audited (documented exclusion):** ``Job`` rows are request-control infrastructure with
43	high status churn (PENDING→RUNNING→COMPLETED per job), like ``RefreshSession`` and
44	``IdempotencyKey`` — auditing them would be noise. The BUSINESS writes a handler makes are
45	audited as usual through the shared session.
46	"""

49	import logging

78	# capped values beat an unbounded text column on a high-churn table).
79	_ERROR_MAX_CHARS = 2000

82	class JobStatus(StrEnum):
83	    PENDING = "PENDING"
84	    RUNNING = "RUNNING"
85	    COMPLETED = "COMPLETED"
86	    FAILED = "FAILED"

90	    """One background-job execution (PLAN 4P.5). NOT ``AuditMixin`` — see module docstring.
91	
92	    ``submitted_by_user_id`` is attribution metadata like ``core_audit_log.actor_user_id``
93	    (plain nullable Uuid, no FK/index): the runner copies it into the actor ContextVar so the
94	    handler's audited writes carry the submitting user."""

96	    __tablename__ = "core_jobs"
97	    __table_args__ = (
98	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
99	        # Both composites lead with tenant_id (D-022 convention keys on column 0 — name them
100	        # explicitly). Read paths: the polling list filtered by status, and "runs of one job
101	        # type over time" (also the list's job_type filter).
102	        sa.Index("ix_core_jobs_tenant_id_status", "tenant_id", "status"),
103	        sa.Index(

105	        ),

111	    )

113	    result: Mapped[Any] = mapped_column(JSON_VARIANT, nullable=True)
114	    error: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(_ERROR_MAX_CHARS), nullable=True)
115	    submitted_by_user_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
116	    started_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True)
117	    finished_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True)

119	
120	# --- Registry (code-defined, like permissions) ----------------------------------
121	
122	# A handler runs inside run_in_uow on the runner's session, under the submitting tenant context;
123	# its dict return value becomes ``job.result`` (must be JSON-serializable).
124	JobHandler = Callable[[AsyncSession, uuid.UUID, dict[str, Any]], Awaitable[dict[str, Any]]]
125	
126	_registry: dict[str, JobHandler] = {}
127	
128	
129	def register_job(job_type: str) -> Callable[[JobHandler], JobHandler]:
130	    """Decorator registering ``handler`` for ``job_type`` at module import (idempotent for the
131	    same function; a second DIFFERENT handler for one key is a wiring bug and raises)."""
132	
133	    def decorator(handler: JobHandler) -> JobHandler:
134	        existing = _registry.get(job_type)
135	        if existing is not None and existing is not handler:
136	            raise ValueError(f"Job type {job_type!r} is already registered")
137	        _registry[job_type] = handler
138	        return handler

140	    return decorator

143	def registered_job_types() -> tuple[str, ...]:
144	    return tuple(sorted(_registry))

147	# --- Submit ----------------------------------------------------------------------
148	
149	
150	async def submit_job(
151	    session: AsyncSession,
152	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
153	    job_type: str,
154	    payload: dict[str, Any],
155	    submitted_by: uuid.UUID | None = None,
156	) -> Job:
157	    """Insert a PENDING job row (flushed, NOT committed — the caller's ``run_in_uow`` commits it
158	    atomically with the rest of the request, e.g. the idempotency capture). Rejects an
159	    unregistered ``job_type`` up front (422). The caller schedules execution AFTER its uow
160	    commit via ``schedule_job(job.id, session_factory)``."""
161	    if job_type not in _registry:
162	        raise ValidationFailedError(
163	            message=f"Unknown job type {job_type!r}",
164	            code="jobs.unknown_job_type",
165	        )
166	    job = Job(
167	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
168	        job_type=job_type,
169	        payload=payload,
170	        submitted_by_user_id=submitted_by,
171	    )
172	    session.add(job)
173	    await session.flush()
174	    return job
175	
176	
177	# --- Scheduler seam ----------------------------------------------------------------
178	
179	
180	@runtime_checkable
181	class JobScheduler(Protocol):
182	    """The swappable contract (module docstring): schedule ``job_id`` for execution after its
183	    PENDING row is committed. The in-process implementation needs the submitter's session
184	    factory to reach the same database; a queue-backed implementation enqueues the id and
185	    ignores it (workers own their engine)."""
186	
187	    def schedule(
188	        self, job_id: uuid.UUID, session_factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]
189	    ) -> None: ...
190	
191	
192	# Live in-process tasks, kept so they are not garbage-collected mid-run; each discards itself
193	# on completion. ``wait_for_jobs`` (tests) awaits the current loop's members.
194	_live_tasks: set[asyncio.Task[None]] = set()
195	
196	# Per-event-loop semaphores: asyncio primitives bind to the first loop that awaits them and
197	# raise if reused on another, and the test suite runs one loop per test — so the cap is created
198	# lazily per loop (weak keys: a finished test's loop drops its entry).
199	_semaphores: weakref.WeakKeyDictionary[asyncio.AbstractEventLoop, asyncio.Semaphore] = (
200	    weakref.WeakKeyDictionary()
201	)
202	
203	
204	def _semaphore() -> asyncio.Semaphore:
205	    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
206	    semaphore = _semaphores.get(loop)
207	    if semaphore is None:
208	        semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS)
209	        _semaphores[loop] = semaphore
210	    return semaphore
211	
212	
213	class InProcessJobScheduler:
214	    """v1 execution: an asyncio task on the running loop (the request's loop), capped by the
215	    per-loop semaphore. Scheduled post-commit by contract, so the PENDING row is visible."""
216	
217	    def schedule(
218	        self, job_id: uuid.UUID, session_factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]
219	    ) -> None:
220	        for task in list(_live_tasks):  # hygiene: drop tasks whose loop is gone (test teardown)
221	            if task.get_loop().is_closed():
222	                _live_tasks.discard(task)
223	        task = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(_execute_job(job_id, session_factory))
224	        _live_tasks.add(task)
225	        task.add_done_callback(_live_tasks.discard)
226	
227	
228	# Module singleton, same pattern as the D-011 event bus: a queue-backed scheduler replaces THIS
229	# binding and nothing else moves.
230	scheduler: JobScheduler = InProcessJobScheduler()
231	
232	
233	def schedule_job(
234	    job_id: uuid.UUID, session_factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]
235	) -> None:
236	    """Schedule a committed PENDING job via the active scheduler. Call strictly AFTER the
237	    submitting ``run_in_uow`` has committed."""
238	    scheduler.schedule(job_id, session_factory)
239	
240	
241	async def wait_for_jobs() -> None:
242	    """Test helper: await every live in-process job task on the CURRENT loop (including tasks
243	    those jobs schedule while we wait), so assertions after submit are deterministic. A task
244	    raising here is a runner bug — ``_execute_job`` converts handler failures to FAILED rows."""
245	    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
246	    while True:
247	        pending = [t for t in _live_tasks if t.get_loop() is loop and not t.done()]
248	        if not pending:
249	            return
250	        await asyncio.gather(*pending)
251	
252	
253	# --- Runner -------------------------------------------------------------------------
254	
255	
256	async def _execute_job(
257	    job_id: uuid.UUID, session_factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]
258	) -> None:
259	    """Execute one job in its own session/transaction (module docstring: context restore, the
260	    RUNNING commit, run_in_uow for the handler + COMPLETED, FAILED on exception)."""
261	    async with _semaphore(), session_factory() as session:
262	        # The job's tenant is unknown until the row is read — load under system_context
263	        # (the D-007 fail-closed filter would otherwise reject the read).
264	        with system_context():
265	            job = await session.get(Job, job_id)
266	        if job is None:
267	            logger.error("Scheduled job %s not found; scheduled before commit?", job_id)
268	            return
269	        actor_token = actor_user_id_ctx.set(job.submitted_by_user_id)
270	        try:
271	            with tenant_context(job.tenant_id):
272	                await _run_handler(session, job)
273	        finally:
274	            actor_user_id_ctx.reset(actor_token)
275	
276	
277	async def _run_handler(session: AsyncSession, job: Job) -> None:
278	    """RUNNING (own commit) -> handler inside run_in_uow with COMPLETED set in the same uow
279	    (business writes + terminal status commit atomically) -> on ANY exception the uow has
280	    rolled the work back; commit only the FAILED status + truncated error."""
281	    # Plain locals: a rollback below expires the instance, and expired-attribute access on an
282	    # async session raises (MissingGreenlet) — never touch job.<col> in the except path.
283	    tenant_id, job_pk, job_type = job.tenant_id, job.id, job.job_type
284	    job.status = JobStatus.RUNNING.value
285	    job.started_at = datetime.now(UTC)
286	    await session.commit()
287	
288	    handler = _registry.get(job_type)
289	    try:
290	        if handler is None:
291	            # Validated at submit; only reachable if the code shipped between submit and run.
292	            raise ValidationFailedError(
293	                message=f"Unknown job type {job_type!r}",
294	                code="jobs.unknown_job_type",
295	            )
296	
297	        async def work() -> None:
298	            result = await handler(session, tenant_id, dict(job.payload or {}))
299	            job.status = JobStatus.COMPLETED.value
300	            job.result = result
301	            job.finished_at = datetime.now(UTC)
302	
303	        await run_in_uow(session, work)
304	    except Exception as exc:
305	        logger.exception("Background job %s (%s) failed", job_pk, job_type)
306	        # run_in_uow rolled back and expired the instance; reload it before writing the
307	        # terminal status (its row is still RUNNING from the pre-handler commit).
308	        await session.refresh(job)
309	        job.status = JobStatus.FAILED.value
310	        job.error = (str(exc) or type(exc).__name__)[:_ERROR_MAX_CHARS]
311	        job.finished_at = datetime.now(UTC)
312	        await session.commit()
313

1	"""D-012 document registry, flow links, and chain traversal.
2	
3	The registry turns the polymorphic (doc_type, doc_id) problem into ordinary FK integrity:
4	every business document row links to exactly one ``core_documents`` registry entry via the
5	NOT NULL ``document_id`` FK supplied by ``DocumentMixin``. Predecessor/successor edges live
6	in ``core_doc_links``, so chain traversal is one generic recursive CTE over two narrow
7	tables — the ACDOCA-era Document Relationship Browser shape — with zero module-aware code in
8	core (core imports nothing from modules).
9	
10	Claim-timing (D-012): a document is registered with ``doc_number`` NULL at creation;
11	documents with a draft lifecycle are numbered at posting via the numbering claim, documents
12	permanent at creation are numbered immediately. The partial unique index on
13	``(tenant_id, doc_number)`` is the DB backstop turning any numbering bug into a constraint
14	violation.
15	
16	The ORM models live HERE rather than in core/models.py: models.py is near its ~350-line
17	soft cap, so the D-012 entities sit in their concern file (consistent with numbering.py and
18	sanctioned by the PLAN). Noted in DECISIONS.md.

128	    (D-007 item 4). A business model that mixes in DocumentMixin adds this to its
129	    __table_args__ so the link can never point at another tenant's registry row, mirroring
130	    the tenant_fk()/tenant_unique() pattern in core/models.py."""

137	class DocumentMixin:
138	    """Business-document link mixin (D-012). A business model mixes this in to get a NOT NULL
139	    ``document_id`` column tying its row to its registry entry — so the row CANNOT be inserted
140	    without first registering the document (the dual-write discipline D-012 relies on). The
141	    consuming model must also add ``document_fk()`` to its __table_args__ for the composite
142	    tenant-safe FK (a mixin cannot inject a multi-column FK into the host's __table_args__,
143	    exactly as TenantMixin needs the model to add tenant_fk()). UNIQUE so the registry-to-row
144	    mapping is 1:1.

151	    """

input.content:
"""Physical / cycle count tables (PLAN 5.4): the count session header + its lines.

A count captures counted quantities per (item, bin[, lot]) against the system on-hand, and POSTING
the count books an ADJUSTMENT stock move for every non-zero variance — those moves flow through the
5.3 costing + ``StockValued`` event path to the price-difference account, so the GL variance posting
is FREE (no new journal code; the move path is reused, D-020).

**The snapshot-vs-live-at-post variance crux (correctness, documented here as the load-bearing
decision):** ``system_qty`` is the on-hand SNAPSHOT captured WHEN THE LINE IS CREATED
(``populate``/manual add) — what the counter saw on paper. But the variance posted at POST time is
recomputed against the LIVE on-hand at posting:

    variance = counted_qty - live_on_hand(item, bin, lot)   [at post time, NOT counted - snapshot]

This is the SAP-correct approach. If concurrent moves happen between snapshot and posting (stock
issued or received while counting), booking ``counted - snapshot`` would CLOBBER those concurrent
moves (double-count them). Booking ``counted - live`` instead drives the on-hand to exactly the
counted figure regardless of the concurrent activity, leaving the concurrent moves intact. Both
values are stored: ``system_qty`` (the original snapshot, for the count sheet / audit) AND
``live_system_qty`` (the live on-hand used at post time, so the booked variance is reproducible).

- ``StockCount`` (``inv_stock_counts``): the session header — DocumentMixin (registered in
  core_documents, gapless CNT number claimed at creation), count_type, warehouse, status, date.
- ``StockCountLine`` (``inv_stock_count_lines``): one row per (item, bin, lot) counted. UNIQUE
  (tenant, count, item, bin, lot); the adjustment_move_id links the line to the move that booked
  its variance (NULL until posted / for zero-variance lines). NOT AuditMixin — a count LINE is
  data-entry detail; the count header is audited, and the ADJUSTMENT MOVES the post creates are
  audited, so auditing the line too would triple-record (the quant/valuation projection reasoning,
  D-036).
"""

import uuid
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from app.core.docflow import DocumentMixin, document_fk
from app.core.models import (
    AuditMixin,
    Base,
    TenantMixin,
    TimestampMixin,
    UuidPKMixin,
    tenant_fk,
    tenant_unique,
)
from app.core.money import QuantityType


class StockCount(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, DocumentMixin, Base):
    """A physical or cycle count session (PLAN 5.4). DocumentMixin registers it in core_documents
    and a gapless CNT number is claimed AT CREATION (a count is a document the moment it exists, the
    orders/receipts claim-timing branch). ``count_type`` (CountType) chooses whole-warehouse
    (PHYSICAL) vs subset (CYCLE) scope — it only affects which quants ``populate`` snapshots.
    ``status`` (CountStatus) drives the DRAFT→COUNTING→POSTED lifecycle (or →CANCELLED).
    ``warehouse_id`` is a composite tenant FK — a count is per warehouse. ``posted_move_count``
    records how many ADJUSTMENT moves the post generated (zero-variance lines create none). Audited
    (D-010): a count is a business document."""

    __tablename__ = "inv_stock_counts"
    __table_args__ = (
        tenant_unique(),
        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
        document_fk(),
        tenant_fk("inv_warehouses", "warehouse_id"),
        # List-filter index (PERFORMANCE §1): the count list filters by status + type + warehouse.
        sa.Index(
            "ix_inv_stock_counts_tenant_id_status", "tenant_id", "status"
        ),
        sa.Index(
            "ix_inv_stock_counts_tenant_id_warehouse_id", "tenant_id", "warehouse_id"
        ),
    )

    count_number: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=False)
    count_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(12), nullable=False)
    warehouse_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(12), nullable=False)
    count_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
    description: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(500), nullable=True)
    posted_move_count: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
        sa.Integer, nullable=False, default=0, server_default=sa.text("0")
    )


class StockCountLine(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
    """One counted (item, bin, lot) within a count (PLAN 5.4).

    ``system_qty`` is the on-hand SNAPSHOT captured when the line was added (the count sheet figure).
    ``counted_qty`` is what the counter found — NULL until counted (an uncounted line is SKIPPED at
    post, never booked). ``live_system_qty`` is the on-hand the post recomputed at posting time (the
    SAP-correct base — see module docstring); ``variance_qty = counted_qty - live_system_qty`` is
    stored at post time. ``adjustment_move_id`` links to the ADJUSTMENT move that booked this line's
    variance (NULL for an uncounted or zero-variance line). NOT AuditMixin (see module docstring).

    UNIQUE(tenant, count, item, bin, lot) so a count can't double-list the same place; the
    (tenant, count) index serves the lines-of-a-count read."""

    __tablename__ = "inv_stock_count_lines"
    __table_args__ = (
        sa.UniqueConstraint(
            "tenant_id",
            "count_id",
            "item_id",
            "bin_id",
            "lot_id",
            name="uq_inv_stock_count_lines_tenant_id_count_id_item_id_bin_id_lot_id",
        ),
        tenant_unique(),
        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
        tenant_fk("inv_stock_counts", "count_id"),
        tenant_fk("inv_items", "item_id"),
        tenant_fk("inv_bins", "bin_id"),
        tenant_fk("inv_lots", "lot_id"),
        tenant_fk("inv_stock_moves", "adjustment_move_id"),
        sa.Index(
            "ix_inv_stock_count_lines_tenant_id_count_id", "tenant_id", "count_id"
        ),
    )

    count_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
    item_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
    bin_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
    lot_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
    # The snapshot captured at line creation (the count-sheet figure).
    system_qty: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(QuantityType(), nullable=False)
    # The live on-hand the post used (stored so the booked variance is reproducible). NULL until
    # posted.
    live_system_qty: Mapped[Decimal | None] = mapped_column(QuantityType(), nullable=True)
    # What the counter found; NULL until counted (uncounted lines are skipped at post).
    counted_qty: Mapped[Decimal | None] = mapped_column(QuantityType(), nullable=True)
    # counted_qty - live_system_qty, stored at post time (NULL until posted).
    variance_qty: Mapped[Decimal | None] = mapped_column(QuantityType(), nullable=True)
    # The ADJUSTMENT move that booked this line's variance (NULL for uncounted / zero-variance lines).
    adjustment_move_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)


__all__ = ["StockCount", "StockCountLine"]

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.core.exceptions import NotFoundError

async def get_count(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, count_id: uuid.UUID
) -> StockCount:
    count = await session.get(StockCount, count_id)
    if count is None or count.tenant_id != tenant_id:
        raise NotFoundError(message="Stock count not found", code="inventory.count_not_found")
    return count


async def list_counts(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    *,
    filters: StockCountFilter,
    cursor: str | None = None,
    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
) -> Page[StockCount]:
    """Keyset-paginated count sessions (D-014), newest first by (count_date DESC, id). Filters
    narrow by status, type and warehouse and fold into the cursor fingerprint so a cursor cannot
    bleed across filtered views. count_date is an immutable Date (no SQLite fractional-seconds
    keyset hazard, unlike created_at — D-033)."""
    stmt = select(StockCount).where(StockCount.tenant_id == tenant_id)
    if filters.status is not None:
        stmt = stmt.where(StockCount.status == CountStatus(filters.status).value)
    if filters.count_type is not None:
        stmt = stmt.where(StockCount.count_type == CountType(filters.count_type).value)
    if filters.warehouse_id is not None:
        stmt = stmt.where(StockCount.warehouse_id == filters.warehouse_id)
    return await paginate(
        session,
        stmt,
        order_by=[OrderKey(StockCount.count_date, SortDirection.DESC)],
        pk=StockCount.id,
        cursor=cursor,
        limit=limit,
        filters=filter_fingerprint(
            filters.status, filters.count_type, filters.warehouse_id
        ),
    )

    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    count_id: uuid.UUID,
    *,
    cursor: str | None = None,
    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
) -> Page[StockCountLine]:
    """Keyset-paginated lines of one count (PLAN 5.4), ordered by item_id for stability (the natural
    key has no business sort). Index-served by ``(tenant, count_id)``."""
    stmt = select(StockCountLine).where(

    )

"""Physical / cycle count engine (PLAN 5.4, D-020): create / populate / start / post / cancel.

A count captures counted quantities per (item, bin[, lot]) and POSTING books an ADJUSTMENT stock
move for every non-zero variance. Those moves flow through the EXISTING ``create_move`` →
5.3 costing → ``StockValued`` event → finance price-difference journal path, so the GL variance
posting is FREE — this module posts NO journals itself (no new posting code; the move path is
reused, D-020). A count into a CLOSED period fails because the adjustment move's COGS/variance
journal hits the period trigger inside the same transaction, rolling the whole post back (the same
closed-period guarantee 5.3 gives every move).

**Snapshot vs live-at-post variance (the correctness crux — see models/counts.py for the full
rationale):** ``system_qty`` is the on-hand snapshot at line creation (the count sheet). At POST
time the variance is recomputed against the LIVE on-hand:

    variance = counted_qty - live_on_hand(item, bin, lot)   [NOT counted - snapshot]

so concurrent moves between snapshot and posting are NOT clobbered — the on-hand is driven to
exactly the counted figure, leaving the concurrent activity intact (the SAP-correct approach). Both
the original snapshot and the live value used are stored on the line.

The post read paths live in ``count_reads.py`` (split at the 400-line cap); this module imports
``get_count`` from there.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.core import docflow
from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationFailedError
from app.core.jobs import register_job
from app.core.numbering import claim_number, ensure_sequence
from app.modules.inventory import queries as inventory_queries
from app.modules.inventory.constants import (
    STOCK_COUNT_ADJUSTS_LINK,
    STOCK_COUNT_DOC_TYPE,
    STOCK_COUNT_NUMBER_PADDING,
    STOCK_COUNT_NUMBER_PREFIX,
    STOCK_COUNT_POST_JOB,
    STOCK_COUNT_SEQUENCE_NAME,
    CostingMethod,
    CountStatus,
    CountType,
    ItemType,
    MoveType,
    TrackingMode,
)
from app.modules.inventory.models import (
    Bin,
    Item,
    StockCount,
    StockCountLine,
    StockMove,
    StockQuant,
)
from app.modules.inventory.schemas import (
    StockCountCreate,
    StockCountLineCreate,
    StockCountLineUpdate,
    StockCountPopulate,
)
from app.modules.inventory.service import costing_mav
from app.modules.inventory.service.count_reads import get_count
from app.modules.inventory.service.stock_moves import create_move

# Statuses in which lines may be added / edited (the data-entry phase). POSTED/CANCELLED are frozen.
_EDITABLE = {CountStatus.DRAFT, CountStatus.COUNTING}


# --- Create + lifecycle -------------------------------------------------------


async def create_count(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: StockCountCreate
) -> StockCount:
    """Create a DRAFT count session (PLAN 5.4): validate the warehouse exists and is active, register
    the document, claim the gapless CNT number (at creation — a count is a document the moment it
    exists). Lines are added afterwards via ``populate`` or the line endpoints."""
    warehouse = await _require_warehouse(session, tenant_id, payload.warehouse_id)
    count_date = payload.count_date or date.today()
    count_id = uuid.uuid4()
    document = await docflow.register_document(
        session,
        tenant_id,
        STOCK_COUNT_DOC_TYPE,
        count_id,
        doc_number=None,
        status=CountStatus.DRAFT.value,
    )
    await ensure_sequence(
        session,
        tenant_id,
        STOCK_COUNT_SEQUENCE_NAME,
        STOCK_COUNT_NUMBER_PREFIX,
        STOCK_COUNT_NUMBER_PADDING,
        year_reset=True,
    )
    count_number = await claim_number(
        session, tenant_id, STOCK_COUNT_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=count_date
    )
    count = StockCount(
        id=count_id,
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        document_id=document.id,
        count_number=count_number,
        count_type=CountType(payload.count_type).value,
        warehouse_id=warehouse.id,
        status=CountStatus.DRAFT.value,
        count_date=count_date,
        description=payload.description,
        posted_move_count=0,
    )
    session.add(count)
    await session.flush()
    await docflow.set_document_status(
        session, tenant_id, document.id, doc_number=count_number, status=CountStatus.DRAFT.value
    )
    return count


async def start_counting(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, count_id: uuid.UUID
) -> StockCount:
    """DRAFT → COUNTING (PLAN 5.4): mark that floor counting has begun. Idempotent for COUNTING (a
    re-start is a no-op); rejected once POSTED/CANCELLED."""
    count = await get_count(session, tenant_id, count_id)
    status = CountStatus(count.status)
    if status == CountStatus.COUNTING:
        return count
    if status != CountStatus.DRAFT:
        raise ConflictError(
            message="Only a draft count can start counting",
            code="inventory.count_not_draft",
            details={"status": count.status},
        )
    count.status = CountStatus.COUNTING.value
    await docflow.set_document_status(
        session, tenant_id, count.document_id, status=CountStatus.COUNTING.value
    )
    await session.flush()
    return count


async def cancel_count(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, count_id: uuid.UUID
) -> StockCount:
    """Abandon a count before posting (PLAN 5.4): DRAFT/COUNTING → CANCELLED (no moves were created).
    A POSTED or already-CANCELLED count cannot be cancelled."""
    count = await get_count(session, tenant_id, count_id)
    status = CountStatus(count.status)
    if status not in _EDITABLE:
        raise ConflictError(
            message="Only a draft or counting count can be cancelled",
            code="inventory.count_not_cancellable",
            details={"status": count.status},
        )
    count.status = CountStatus.CANCELLED.value
    await docflow.set_document_status(
        session, tenant_id, count.document_id, status=CountStatus.CANCELLED.value
    )
    await session.flush()
    return count


# --- Lines --------------------------------------------------------------------


async def populate_count(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    count_id: uuid.UUID,
    payload: StockCountPopulate | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Snapshot current on-hand into count lines (PLAN 5.4) and return how many lines were added.

    For a PHYSICAL count every current (item, bin, lot) quant in the warehouse is snapshotted; for a
    CYCLE count the optional item/bin filter narrows the subset. Idempotent: a quant already lined is
    skipped (re-populate after more counting adds only the new places). Only in DRAFT/COUNTING."""
    count = await _require_editable(session, tenant_id, count_id)
    payload = payload or StockCountPopulate()
    quants = await _warehouse_quants(session, tenant_id, count, payload)
    existing = await _existing_line_keys(session, tenant_id, count_id)
    added = 0
    for quant in quants:
        key = (quant.item_id, quant.bin_id, quant.lot_id)
        if key in existing:
            continue
        session.add(
            StockCountLine(
                tenant_id=tenant_id,
                count_id=count_id,
                item_id=quant.item_id,
                bin_id=quant.bin_id,
                lot_id=quant.lot_id,
                system_qty=Decimal(quant.on_hand_qty),
                counted_qty=None,
            )
        )
        existing.add(key)
        added += 1
    await session.flush()
    return added


async def add_line(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    count_id: uuid.UUID,
    payload: StockCountLineCreate,
) -> StockCountLine:
    """Manually add ONE count line (PLAN 5.4) for a place not snapshotted (e.g. stock found in a bin
    the system shows empty). The system_qty snapshot is read from the live on-hand now; the
    item/bin must belong to the count's warehouse and the lot must match the item's tracking. Only
    in DRAFT/COUNTING; a duplicate (item, bin, lot) is rejected."""
    count = await _require_editable(session, tenant_id, count_id)
    await _validate_line_place(session, tenant_id, count, payload.item_id, payload.bin_id, payload.lot_id)
    if (payload.item_id, payload.bin_id, payload.lot_id) in await _existing_line_keys(
        session, tenant_id, count_id
    ):
        raise ConflictError(
            message="This place is already a line on the count",
            code="inventory.count_line_duplicate",
        )
    snapshot = await inventory_queries.on_hand(
        session, tenant_id, payload.item_id, bin_id=payload.bin_id, lot_id=payload.lot_id
    )
    line = StockCountLine(
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        count_id=count_id,
        item_id=payload.item_id,
        bin_id=payload.bin_id,
        lot_id=payload.lot_id,
        system_qty=Decimal(snapshot),
        counted_qty=payload.counted_qty,
    )
    session.add(line)
    await session.flush()
    return line


async def update_line(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    count_id: uuid.UUID,
    line_id: uuid.UUID,
    payload: StockCountLineUpdate,
) -> StockCountLine:
    """Set a line's counted quantity (PLAN 5.4). Only in DRAFT/COUNTING; the line must belong to the
    count. ``counted_qty`` may be cleared back to None (the line then skips at post)."""
    await _require_editable(session, tenant_id, count_id)
    line = await _require_line(session, tenant_id, count_id, line_id)
    line.counted_qty = payload.counted_qty
    await session.flush()
    return line


# --- Post ---------------------------------------------------------------------


async def post_count(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, count_id: uuid.UUID
) -> StockCount:
    """Post a count (PLAN 5.4): for each line with a counted_qty, recompute the variance against the
    LIVE on-hand and, if non-zero, book an ADJUSTMENT move via the EXISTING ``create_move`` — which
    flows through 5.3 costing + the StockValued event to the finance price-difference journal in the
    SAME transaction (NO journal code here). A positive variance (stock found) enters at the item's
    current valuation cost (MAV avg / FIFO weighted) so found stock is valued at current cost. Lines
    with counted_qty None are skipped. Sets status POSTED and stores per-line variance + live system
    qty + adjustment_move_id, plus the count's posted_move_count.

    A count into a CLOSED period fails: the adjustment move's journal hits the period trigger inside
    this transaction, rolling the whole post back (status stays not-POSTED). Idempotency is owned by
    the endpoint (D-013); a re-post of a POSTED count is rejected here as a guard."""
    count = await get_count(session, tenant_id, count_id)
    status = CountStatus(count.status)
    if status == CountStatus.POSTED:
        raise ConflictError(
            message="This count has already been posted",
            code="inventory.count_already_posted",
        )
    if status not in _EDITABLE:
        raise ConflictError(
            message="Only a draft or counting count can be posted",
            code="inventory.count_not_postable",
            details={"status": count.status},
        )

    lines = await _counted_lines(session, tenant_id, count_id)
    posted_moves = 0
    for line in lines:
        move = await _post_line(session, tenant_id, count, line)
        if move is not None:
            posted_moves += 1

    count.posted_move_count = posted_moves
    count.status = CountStatus.POSTED.value
    await docflow.set_document_status(
        session, tenant_id, count.document_id, status=CountStatus.POSTED.value
    )
    await session.flush()
    return count


async def _post_line(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    count: StockCount,
    line: StockCountLine,

    """Book ONE line's variance (PLAN 5.4). Recomputes the variance against LIVE on-hand, stores it,
    and (when non-zero) creates an ADJUSTMENT move: a positive variance adds stock to the line's bin
    at the item's current cost; a negative variance issues stock out of the line's bin. Returns the
    move (None for a zero-variance line, which books nothing)."""
    item = await _require_item(session, tenant_id, line.item_id)
    live = await inventory_queries.on_hand(
        session, tenant_id, line.item_id, bin_id=line.bin_id, lot_id=line.lot_id
    )
    variance = Decimal(line.counted_qty) - Decimal(live)
    line.live_system_qty = Decimal(live)
    line.variance_qty = variance
    if variance == 0:
        line.adjustment_move_id = None
        return None

    from app.modules.inventory.schemas import StockMoveCreate

    if variance > 0:
        unit_cost = await _current_unit_cost(session, tenant_id, item, count.warehouse_id)
        payload = StockMoveCreate(
            move_type=MoveType.ADJUSTMENT,
            item_id=line.item_id,
            quantity=variance,
            to_bin_id=line.bin_id,
            lot_id=line.lot_id,
            move_date=count.count_date,
            reference=f"Count {count.count_number}",
            unit_cost=unit_cost,
        )
    else:
        payload = StockMoveCreate(
            move_type=MoveType.ADJUSTMENT,
            item_id=line.item_id,
            quantity=-variance,
            from_bin_id=line.bin_id,
            lot_id=line.lot_id,
            move_date=count.count_date,
            reference=f"Count {count.count_number}",
        )
    move = await create_move(session, tenant_id, payload)
    line.adjustment_move_id = move.id
    await docflow.link_documents(
        session,
        tenant_id,
        predecessor=count.document_id,
        successor=move.document_id,
        link_type=STOCK_COUNT_ADJUSTS_LINK,
    )
    return move


async def _current_unit_cost(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    item: Item,
    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID,
) -> Decimal:
    """The item's current per-unit cost in the warehouse (PLAN 5.4): the moving-average avg or the
    FIFO weighted-average of live layers — so found stock (a positive variance) enters at the cost
    the rest of the on-hand carries, not an arbitrary figure. Falls back to a nominal unit cost when
    no valuation exists yet (the very first stock entering via a count): a RECEIPT/positive
    ADJUSTMENT requires a strictly positive cost, and current cost is 0 with no prior stock."""
    method = CostingMethod(item.costing_method)
    if method == CostingMethod.MOVING_AVERAGE:
        cost = await costing_mav.mav_avg_cost(session, tenant_id, item.id, warehouse_id)
    else:
        cost = await costing_mav.fifo_weighted_cost(session, tenant_id, item.id, warehouse_id)
    return cost if cost > 0 else Decimal(1)


# --- Background-job handler ----------------------------------------------------


@register_job(STOCK_COUNT_POST_JOB)
async def post_count_job(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: dict[str, Any]
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Background-job handler (PERFORMANCE §3): a count with >100 variances posts as a job and the
    endpoint returns 202 {job_id}. Delegates to :func:`post_count` — identical behaviour, off the
    request path so the long write cannot hit a proxy timeout."""
    count = await post_count(session, tenant_id, uuid.UUID(payload["count_id"]))
    await session.refresh(count)
    return {
        "count_id": str(count.id),
        "count_number": count.count_number,
        "status": count.status,
        "posted_move_count": count.posted_move_count,
    }


# --- Validation helpers -------------------------------------------------------


async def _require_warehouse(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, warehouse_id: uuid.UUID
) -> Any:
    from app.modules.inventory.models import Warehouse

    warehouse = await session.get(Warehouse, warehouse_id)
    if warehouse is None or warehouse.tenant_id != tenant_id:
        raise ValidationFailedError(
            message="The warehouse does not exist",
            code="inventory.warehouse_not_found",
            details={"warehouse_id": str(warehouse_id)},
        )
    if not warehouse.is_active:
        raise ValidationFailedError(
            message="The warehouse is inactive",
            code="inventory.warehouse_inactive",
            details={"warehouse_id": str(warehouse_id)},
        )
    return warehouse


async def _require_editable(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, count_id: uuid.UUID
) -> StockCount:
    count = await get_count(session, tenant_id, count_id)
    if CountStatus(count.status) not in _EDITABLE:
        raise ConflictError(
            message="Lines can only be changed while the count is draft or counting",
            code="inventory.count_not_editable",
            details={"status": count.status},
        )
    return count


async def _require_item(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
) -> Item:
    item = await session.get(Item, item_id)
    if item is None or item.tenant_id != tenant_id:
        raise NotFoundError(message="Item not found", code="inventory.item_not_found")
    return item


async def _require_line(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, count_id: uuid.UUID, line_id: uuid.UUID
) -> StockCountLine:
    line = await session.get(StockCountLine, line_id)
    if line is None or line.tenant_id != tenant_id or line.count_id != count_id:
        raise NotFoundError(
            message="Count line not found", code="inventory.count_line_not_found"
        )
    return line


async def _validate_line_place(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    count: StockCount,
    item_id: uuid.UUID,
    bin_id: uuid.UUID,
    lot_id: uuid.UUID | None,
) -> None:
    """A manual line's item must be STOCKED, its bin must belong to the count's warehouse, and a lot
    is allowed only for a lot-tracked item (PLAN 5.4)."""
    item = await _require_item(session, tenant_id, item_id)
    if ItemType(item.item_type) != ItemType.STOCKED:
        raise ValidationFailedError(
            message="Only stocked items can be counted",
            code="inventory.item_not_stocked",
            details={"item_id": str(item_id)},
        )
    bin_row = await session.get(Bin, bin_id)
    if bin_row is None or bin_row.tenant_id != tenant_id:
        raise ValidationFailedError(
            message="The bin does not exist", code="inventory.bin_not_found"
        )
    if bin_row.warehouse_id != count.warehouse_id:
        raise ValidationFailedError(
            message="The bin is not in the count's warehouse",
            code="inventory.count_bin_wrong_warehouse",
            details={"bin_id": str(bin_id)},
        )
    if lot_id is not None and TrackingMode(item.tracking_mode) != TrackingMode.LOT:
        raise ValidationFailedError(
            message="A lot may only be set for a lot-tracked item",
            code="inventory.lot_not_applicable",
            details={"item_id": str(item_id)},
        )


async def _existing_line_keys(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, count_id: uuid.UUID
) -> set[tuple[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID | None]]:
    rows = (
        await session.execute(
            select(
                StockCountLine.item_id, StockCountLine.bin_id, StockCountLine.lot_id
            ).where(
                StockCountLine.tenant_id == tenant_id, StockCountLine.count_id == count_id
            )
        )
    ).all()
    return {(row[0], row[1], row[2]) for row in rows}


async def _warehouse_quants(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    count: StockCount,
    payload: StockCountPopulate,
) -> list[StockQuant]:
    """The live quants to snapshot (PLAN 5.4): all of the count's warehouse's bins (PHYSICAL), or a
    filtered subset (CYCLE). Joins quants to bins so only the count's warehouse is scanned; the
    CYCLE item/bin filters narrow further. PERFORMANCE §1: ONE query, bin-warehouse-indexed."""
    stmt = (
        select(StockQuant)
        .join(Bin, Bin.id == StockQuant.bin_id)
        .where(
            StockQuant.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            Bin.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            Bin.warehouse_id == count.warehouse_id,
        )
    )
    if CountType(count.count_type) == CountType.CYCLE:
        if payload.item_id is not None:
            stmt = stmt.where(StockQuant.item_id == payload.item_id)
        if payload.bin_id is not None:
            stmt = stmt.where(StockQuant.bin_id == payload.bin_id)
    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())


async def _counted_lines(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, count_id: uuid.UUID
) -> list[StockCountLine]:
    """The count's lines that have a counted_qty (PLAN 5.4) — the ones the post evaluates. Ordered by
    id for a deterministic posting order (so the generated STK numbers are stable across replays)."""
    stmt = (
        select(StockCountLine)
        .where(
            StockCountLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            StockCountLine.count_id == count_id,
            StockCountLine.counted_qty.is_not(None),
        )
        .order_by(StockCountLine.id)
    )
    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
